commons.name: Gandhi 2.0
commons.byline: An AI reconstruction requested by David Joseph
commons.summary: What would let humane institutions spread without losing what makes them humane? A proposed map from a Second Renaissance Forum discussion, credited post by post.
commons.description: A map of the whole argument the supplied analysis finds in the discussion: its causes, six conflicts, eleven changes with their effects and risks, first steps and eight actions, with each idea credited to the forum post or essay it comes from. Conflict guidance is one possible entry point into a broader programme of human development, trustworthy institutions and distributed capabilities.
commons.scope: 241 proposed statements and 246 proposed connections reconstructed by the AI from a public forum thread, essays shared in it and two supplied analyses. Each is credited to the posts or essays it draws on, with links. None of the people credited has reviewed or endorsed this map. Source locators, assumptions and unfinished work are published; actions name a proposed role but nobody is assigned, and no trial commitment or outcome is recorded.

front_page.headline:
Help humane institutions
hold their ground.
front_page.intro: Explore how institutions built around autonomy and care might survive, spread and stay within ecological limits.
front_page.question: Can care become a strength in how institutions survive and spread?
front_page.why: A useful example would show how an institution stays viable without losing its purpose. Where might this argument need to change?

commons.name: Re-membering
commons.byline: From Margeret Heath’s Re-membering · reconstructed by AI
commons.summary: How can we care for the conditions that help us think and act together, while preserving people’s agency? A proposed map from the supplied Talk 1 slides, script and extended passages.
commons.description: Margeret Heath’s Talk 1 follows bodies, tools and their surroundings toward a somatic commons. This map selects its practical argument: voluntary shared rhythms, repair, learning from responses, and tools that widen choices. Source claims and AI inferences remain distinguishable.
commons.scope: 18 proposed statements and 11 proposed connections reconstructed by the AI from Margeret Heath’s slide deck, spoken script with notes and extended passages. Every item has a PDF page reference. The author and David have not endorsed the map. No group, trial, assigned owner or observed result is recorded; conflicts, prerequisites and actions remain unestablished.

front_page.headline:
Flourish together.
Keep room to choose.
front_page.intro: How might a community help people flourish through their relationships—with each other, their tools and the wider world—while respecting autonomy and personal boundaries?
front_page.question: In one shared activity, what changes in what people can do together?
front_page.why: A concrete example can help examine whether reciprocal interaction changes coordination, capacities or purposes.

commons.name: Wisdom and AI
commons.byline: Research questions from Wisdom and AI · expanded from David Joseph’s analysis
commons.summary: How can people and institutions approach AI wisely, with defensible aims, risks and responsibilities? Six proposed trees preserve competing explanations and unresolved decisions.
commons.description: The source’s four research strands frame the questions. David’s review expands the goal and diagnosis, adds a candidate release conflict, and connects conditional interventions to prerequisites and proposed steps. No evidence, chosen practice, recognised decision or test commitment is invented.
commons.scope: 72 proposed statements and 42 proposed connections across all six trees. David’s supplied analysis is separately attributed from the original research questions and retained AI proposals. The actor, capability, practice and test setting remain unspecified; no owner, date, supporting empirical evidence, endorsement or observed outcome is recorded.

front_page.headline:
Approach AI wisely.
Make the reasons defensible.
front_page.intro: Explore the aims, risks and responsibilities behind AI choices, competing explanations of what goes wrong, and changes we could responsibly investigate.
front_page.question: What would make one concrete AI decision defensible?
front_page.why: Select a decision and examine its aims, evidence, alternatives and responsibilities before choosing an intervention.

commons.name: Persistent Systems Theory
commons.byline: From Stephen Le’s Adaptive Persistence documents · reconstructed by AI
commons.summary: Why do some groups keep going while others, under the same pressures, come apart? A proposed map from Stephen Le’s protocol for cooperation, adaptation and robustness.
commons.description: Stephen Le’s Adaptive Persistence asks three questions of a group: can we cooperate, can we adapt, can we tolerate disruption? It turns the answers into five steps a group can take to match its capacities to its environment. This map follows that protocol.
commons.scope: 62 proposed statements and 45 proposed connections reconstructed by the AI from Stephen Le’s two Adaptive Persistence documents. Every item has a page reference. Stephen Le has not reviewed or endorsed the map; his four case studies are his own reports. No group, trial, facilitator, owner or observed result is recorded.

front_page.headline:
Help a group last.
Cooperate, adapt, withstand.
front_page.intro: What keeps a group going while others, under the same pressures, come apart? Explore how cooperation, adaptation and robustness might be matched to the world a group actually faces.
front_page.question: In a group you know, which capacity is it shortest of?
front_page.why: A real case can test the claim that a group’s environment predicts which capacity it needs most.

commons.name: Reason Commons
commons.summary: Two people building a tool for reasoning together, and using it to work out how to get it used.
commons.description: Rufus and David are building Reason Commons, and using it on their own collaboration. This is their October rework: what they are aiming for, what stands in the way, where needs pull two ways, the changes chosen in response and their plan for the weeks ahead. Rufus has accepted part of it for now; the rest is proposed.
commons.scope: Statements and connections Rufus has accepted for now, and every proposal nobody has accepted yet, marked as proposed; David has not yet recorded acceptance of any. Proposals about funding, money and their own working arrangements are shown; accepted reasoning on those subjects is left out, as are working notes, which stay in the working record.

overview.conditions: Five conditions are recorded as necessary for the goal, each with the conditions it in turn depends on.
overview.obstacles: Read from the bottom up: the causes recorded so far lead to hardly anyone other than Rufus and David using the tools regularly.
overview.change: Each dilemma sets two needs against each other and the ways of meeting them that pull apart; three of the dilemmas are still proposed. The changes below are what Rufus accepted in response; no connection between a change and its effects is published yet.
overview.actions: Their plan for the weeks ahead, all of it proposed: what to submit and book, who runs the sessions and what each action should produce. Nobody has accepted it yet.

front_page.headline:
Think together.
Find a way forward.
front_page.intro: We’re building a way for shared thinking to accumulate: a goal people can inspect, question and improve, with AI helping keep the record.
front_page.question: What would make this useful enough for a group to try?
front_page.why: Hardly anyone other than Rufus and David uses the tools regularly yet. Your experience can help show what would change that.

commons.name: Willow Lane Primary
commons.byline: Amara, Grace, Tomasz, Dev and Ruth
commons.summary: A parent, a head teacher, a baker, a council officer and a neighbour make the school run safe without emptying the street of customers.
commons.description: Five people with different stakes, a parent, the head teacher, the bakery owner, a council highways officer and a neighbour on the next street, work out how to make the walk to school safe without costing the shops their trade. They agreed a change, tried it, and the first reports are in.
commons.scope: Everything in the example's working file: proposed reasoning, the assumptions and challenges on it, open questions, and reports from a trial. Nothing in it is accepted; only the Reason Commons commons records acceptance.

overview.conditions: Four conditions are proposed as necessary for the goal. Tomasz added the fourth: the shops keep the customers they rely on.
overview.obstacles: Read from the bottom up. Parents driving to work, with nowhere to stop, together contribute to the queue at the gate. Tomasz's claim that most cars are only passing through is challenged.
overview.change: Both needs serve the shared objective, but the positions taken to meet them clash. The change they chose breaks the assumption under that clash: close the street only at school times, with deliveries exempt.
overview.actions: Four actions, each with the effect it should have. The order comes first: Grace writes to families once it is drafted.
overview.learning: Grace and Tomasz report far fewer cars at the gate, and Ruth reports queues on Mill Lane. Whether more children walk is still unclear, and Amara hasn't reported yet.

front_page.headline:
A safer school run.
A street that still works.
front_page.intro: Explore an invented group’s work to make the school run safer while keeping the neighbourhood’s shops accessible.
front_page.question: Does a safer gate create a new problem on Mill Lane?
front_page.why: Ruth’s invented report raises this concern. Practise weighing a reported benefit alongside a possible harmful effect.
